text:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT 2026-03-23 resolved — brief: sudden synchronized KV TTL expiries + a bad config push caused a cache-miss surge and p99 latency spike. Immediate mitigations: rollback + targeted priming. PM draft: https://redwood.link/pm-1771409012

Jules SRE: adding follow-ups from PM: 1) prevent TTL alignment, 2) add early-warning alerts for miss-rate derivative, 3) update SLO/windowing to better capture tail behavior.

Marco (eng-runtime): root cause confirmed: deploy disabled prefix caching in one cluster and a cron reset TTLs. I have a branch to add jittered TTLs + cap on concurrent origin fetches. Will open PR.

Dani (product): customers saw timeouts on some long routes. Recommendation: keep public SLA unchanged for now; update internal SLOs and product alerts. If repeats >=2 in 30d, escalate SLA review.

Rae (observability): proposed tasks:
- Early-warning alert: 5m derivative on cache_miss_ratio -> owner: Rae -> due: 2026-03-26
- Dashboard: per-region TTL expiry heatmap + 30d rolling p99 -> owner: Rae -> due: 2026-03-28
- Retro lookback for similar incidents (180d window) -> owner: Rae -> due: 2026-03-25

Nina (eng-sre lead): SLO proposal: keep p50/p95, change p99 to rolling 30d window (target 300ms). Alert when 7-day burn > 1.5x baseline or remaining error budget < 25%. Add product notification at 20% remaining. Owner: Nina -> RFC due 2026-03-27.

Jules SRE: runbook checklist I'll add (short): identify hot routes, run priming job, rollback steps. Example prime command below.
```bash
redwoodctl cache prime --region eu-west-2 --routes-file /tmp/hot.txt --parallel 6
```

Marco (eng-runtime): opened draft PR: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/470 — jittered-ttls + fetch-cap. Adding canary that applies cache config to one zone first. Due: 2026-03-31.

Rae (observability): I'll post retro query results by 2026-03-25 and wire alerts to #eng-oncall.

Nina (eng-sre lead): weekly check-ins on Fridays until all items closed. Do not change public SLA today. Tag me if blocked. :thumbsup:
